title: Is a four-day work week worth it?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Welcome back. Today's question: is a four-day work week actually worth it, or is it just a nice idea on paper?

turns.speaker: sam
turns.text: I used to be skeptical. Fewer days sounds like less work done. But the pilot programs I have read about suggest people often keep their output.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: The usual explanation is focus. When the week is shorter, meetings shrink and people protect their time more carefully.

turns.speaker: sam
turns.text: Right, but it is not free. Some jobs, like support or healthcare, need coverage every day, so the schedule has to be designed, not just announced.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: And a compressed week of long days is not the same thing. Four ten-hour days can leave people more tired, not less.

turns.speaker: sam
turns.text: So the honest answer is: it depends on the work. Where output can be measured and shifts can be arranged, it is worth testing.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Test it, measure it, and be ready to adjust. Thanks for listening, and tell us what your team would do with a free Friday.
